chunks: weigh yourselves before you are weighed, and assess yourselves before you are assessed. Breathe before the constriction of the throat, and submit before the harsh driving,
and know that whoever is not helped by himself until he has from himself an adviser and a warner, will not have from others a warner or an adviser.

key_terms.تَزْكِيَة: Self-purification or weighing of the soul
key_terms.زَاجِر: Warner or one who restrains from sin
key_terms.ضِيقُ الْخَنَاقِ: Constriction of the throat, referring to death or the grave
key_terms.عُنْفُ السِّيَاقِ: Harsh driving or compulsion, referring to being led to judgment
key_terms.وَاعِظ: Adviser or one who gives moral counsel

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to weigh and assess oneself before being weighed and assessed?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited in Shia ethical discourse as the foundation of *muhasabat al-nafs* (self-accounting), urges proactive spiritual preparation before the inevitable reckoning of the Hereafter. It highlights the necessity of internalizing divine guidance so that the soul becomes its own witness and judge, a concept deeply rooted in the Shia emphasis on individual responsibility and the refinement of character (*akhlaq*) prior to the final judgment.
